title: Wuthering Heights
synopsis: Two souls, one wild stretch of moorland, and a love that refuses to behave. Choose between the heart and the world — and learn that the moor keeps every choice you make on it.

nodes.text: You and Heathcliff run wild across the moor as children, the wind in your teeth, the world below not yet able to touch you. Up here there are no names, no fathers, no class. Down at the Grange, the lights are coming on.

choices.text: Stay out on the moor till dark
choices.consequence: The wild hours are the only honest ones. You commit to stay out on the moor till dark. By Two Halves, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

choices.text: Go down toward the Grange's warm windows
choices.consequence: Comfort has a gravity all its own. You choose to go down toward the Grange's warm windows. The way to The Grange opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: "I am Heathcliff," you tell yourself, half a prayer. He's not your brother and not your servant and not allowed to be your love, and so of course he is all the air there is. The household already disapproves.

choices.text: Swear nothing will ever part you
choices.consequence: Vows on the moor are heard by the wind alone. You swear nothing will ever part you. It carries you toward The Master's Cruelty and makes the feeling underneath the decision impossible to hide.

choices.text: Keep the bond a guarded secret
choices.consequence: What's hidden grows teeth. You keep the bond a guarded secret. It carries you toward The Proposal and makes the feeling underneath the decision impossible to hide.

nodes.text: The Lintons' house is everything the Heights is not — soft carpets, soft voices, Edgar Linton's soft hopeful eyes on you. A part of you, the part that gets cold and tired, leans toward it. “Let Edgar court you” draws you toward The Proposal; “Refuse the Grange and run back uphill” leaves The Master's Cruelty waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Let Edgar court you
choices.consequence: The warm road is also a road away. You commit to let Edgar court you. By The Proposal, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

choices.text: Refuse the Grange and run back uphill
choices.consequence: Some warmth costs more than the cold. You commit to refuse the Grange and run back uphill. By The Master's Cruelty, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

nodes.text: After the old master dies, Hindley reigns at the Heights and grinds Heathcliff down to a stable hand, beaten and brilliant and burning. You watch the boy you love turned to a servant before your eyes.

choices.text: Defy Hindley openly for Heathcliff
choices.consequence: Open defiance is brave and brittle. You commit to defy Hindley openly for Heathcliff. By The Storm, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

choices.text: Protect Heathcliff in secret
choices.consequence: Quiet shields hold longer than loud ones. You protect Heathcliff in secret. It carries you toward The Years Between and makes the feeling underneath the decision impossible to hide.

nodes.text: Edgar Linton asks for your hand and a future of ease and respectability. You confess to the housekeeper that you love Heathcliff to your bones — but that marrying him now would 'degrade you.' Heathcliff hears only the first half before he flees into the storm.

choices.text: Run after him into the storm
choices.consequence: Chase the truth before pride buries it. You run after him into the storm. It carries you toward The Storm and makes the feeling underneath the decision impossible to hide.

choices.text: Let him go and accept Edgar
choices.consequence: The world is heavy and you are tired of fighting it. You choose to let him go and accept Edgar. The way to Lady of the Grange opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: The moor in a storm is a living thing, and you cannot find him in it. By dawn Heathcliff is gone — vanished entirely, swallowed by the rain and his own wounded pride. The silence he leaves is louder than any wind.

choices.text: Wait years for his return
choices.consequence: Hope is a long and ruinous tenant. You choose to wait years for his return. The way to The Years Between opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Marry Edgar to forget the ache
choices.consequence: Forgetting is a house you can never quite furnish. You commit to marry Edgar to forget the ache. By Lady of the Grange, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

nodes.text: Time passes thin and grey. You become someone's wife or someone's ghost, you're no longer sure which. Then a stranger arrives at the gate — gentlemanly, wealthy, and unmistakably him. Heathcliff has come back rich, and changed.

choices.text: Greet him with open joy
choices.consequence: Joy is honest and dangerous. You commit to greet him with open joy. By He Returns, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

choices.text: Greet him with careful distance
choices.consequence: Caution comes too late to save you. You choose to greet him with careful distance. The way to The Revenge Begins opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: You are mistress of Thrushcross Grange now, fine and admired and slowly starving in a way no meal can fix. Edgar is gentle and good and not enough, and you've begun to fade like a flower kept indoors.

choices.text: Confess your unhappiness to Edgar
choices.consequence: Honesty is a knife you turn on yourself. You choose to confess your unhappiness to Edgar. The way to He Returns opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Hide the sickness of your heart
choices.consequence: What you swallow does not digest. You choose to hide the sickness of your heart. The way to The Revenge Begins opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: Heathcliff is back and he has not forgiven — not you, not Hindley, not the world that ranked him below it. He looks at you with love and ruin in the same glance, and you understand he intends to collect on every old debt.

choices.text: Beg him to choose love over revenge
choices.consequence: Plead with a storm and see what it answers. You choose to beg him to choose love over revenge. The way to The Last Meeting opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Match his cold and play the game
choices.consequence: Two proud people make a long winter. You choose to match his cold and play the game. The way to The Fever opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: He marries Edgar's sister Isabella purely to wound — courting her cruelty by cruelty, ruining a girl who never harmed him, all to put a blade in your peace. The moor watches and keeps its counsel.

choices.text: Try to save Isabella from him
choices.consequence: Mercy aimed at the innocent is never wasted. You choose to try to save Isabella from him. The way to The Last Meeting opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Let him have his terrible victory
choices.consequence: Looking away is its own kind of cruelty. You let him have his terrible victory. It carries you toward The Fever and makes the feeling underneath the decision impossible to hide.

nodes.text: You meet once more, in a room that feels like the edge of a cliff. He holds you and rages at you in the same breath: 'Why did you betray your own heart?' There's no answer that doesn't break something.

choices.text: Tell him the whole, ruinous truth
choices.consequence: Truth, this late, is a wound and a gift. You choose to tell him the whole, ruinous truth. The way to Haunting opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Tell him to live, even without you
choices.consequence: Releasing him is the cruelest love. You choose to tell him to live, even without you. The way to The Long Revenge opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: Grief makes you ill — a fever of the body that is really a fever of the soul, refusing to choose between two impossible lives. You stand at the window calling for the moor, for the wind, for the wild girl you used to be.

choices.text: Reach for the window and the moor
choices.consequence: The heath calls its own home. You choose to reach for the window and the moor. The way to Haunting opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Sink back and let the warm room win
choices.consequence: Sometimes the body decides for you. You choose to sink back and let the warm room win. The way to The Long Revenge opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: Whatever passes between you, it does not end at death — it cannot. You become a presence on the moor, a knock at a window, a name the wind keeps saying. Heathcliff, alive, becomes the truly haunted one.

choices.text: Haunt him until he follows you
choices.consequence: Love that won't die becomes a summons. You choose to haunt him until he follows you. The way to He Stops Eating opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Watch over the next generation instead
choices.consequence: Even ghosts can choose tenderness. You commit to watch over the next generation instead. By The Young Ones, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

nodes.text: Years roll on and Heathcliff, joyless and rich, ruins everyone you both once knew — Hindley's son, Edgar's daughter, his own boy. Revenge has eaten everything, including the parts of him you loved. He is master of two houses and prisoner of one grave.

choices.text: Let the next generation break the curse
choices.consequence: The young are the only escape from the old. You commit to let the next generation break the curse. By The Young Ones, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

choices.text: Let the cruelty run to its bitter end
choices.consequence: Some fires must burn down to the stone. You choose to let the cruelty run to its bitter end. The way to He Stops Eating opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: Near the end, Heathcliff sees you everywhere — in doorways, on the heath, at the foot of his bed. He stops eating, stops sleeping, walks the moor at night calling a name. He is not afraid of his ghost. He is running toward it.

choices.text: Lead him gently to the moor at last
choices.consequence: Death, for some, is the only reunion left. You lead him gently to the moor at last. It carries you toward The Last Walk and makes the feeling underneath the decision impossible to hide.

choices.text: Make him pay for every cruelty first
choices.consequence: Even love can curdle into justice. You choose to make him pay for every cruelty first. The way to A Cruel Calm opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: Cathy's daughter and Hindley's son — raised in the wreckage you and Heathcliff left behind — begin, impossibly, to teach each other to read, to be gentle, to love without ruin. The moor, for once, is kind.

choices.text: Bless the young lovers from the wind
choices.consequence: The best revenge on the past is a better future. You choose to bless the young lovers from the wind. The way to Letters Across the Moor opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Watch over the heath itself, eternal
choices.consequence: Some loves become the land itself. You watch over the heath itself, eternal. It carries you toward The Wind Speaks and makes the feeling underneath the decision impossible to hide.

nodes.text: You guide him out one final dawn, across the heather you ran on as children. The path narrows. He stops calling your name aloud because he no longer has to — you are walking beside him at last.

choices.text: Take his hand as the light comes up
choices.consequence: After a lifetime apart, the simplest gesture. You commit to take his hand as the light comes up. By Two Graves, One Heath, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

choices.text: Step ahead and let him follow at his own pace
choices.consequence: Even reunion can be a thing you walk gently into. You commit to step ahead and let him follow at his own pace. By Two Graves, One Heath, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

nodes.text: You refuse him. The window stays shut. He paces the moor for nights and finds no door home, no rest, no you. Justice and love look the same from a distance, and yours is being measured from a distance now.

choices.text: Hold the cold a little longer
choices.consequence: Hardness can be its own grief. You choose to hold the cold a little longer. The way to The Unquiet opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Soften at the very last moment
choices.consequence: A cracked door is still mercy. You commit to soften at the very last moment. By Two Graves, One Heath, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

nodes.text: The young lovers leave small offerings on the heath without quite knowing why — a ribbon, a stone, a sprig of heather. You feel each one. The wind, gentler now, carries your approval back in directions only the bees take seriously.

choices.text: Let them feel watched over, kindly
choices.consequence: Some hauntings are blessings in disguise. You choose to let them feel watched over, kindly. The way to A Gentler Heath opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Step back so they can write their own story
choices.consequence: The greatest love is the one that gets out of the way. You commit to step back so they can write their own story. By A Gentler Heath, the distance between you will have changed, even if neither of you names it.

nodes.text: Time wears down the houses, the wrongs, the names. What remains is wind, water, heather, and the long memory of a girl and a boy who ran wild here. Travelers say they can hear you laughing on storm-nights. They are right.

choices.text: Settle fully into the moor
choices.consequence: Some homes choose to keep you. You choose to settle fully into the moor. The way to I Am the Moor opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

choices.text: Move on at last, satisfied
choices.consequence: Even ghosts can finish their story. You choose to move on at last, satisfied. The way to A Gentler Heath opens, trading the safety of ambiguity for the possibility of being understood.

nodes.text: They bury him beside you, and the villagers swear that on wild nights two figures walk the moor, finally at peace because they are finally past the world that kept them apart. You are not in heaven or hell. You are home, in the wind, together.

He dies reaching for a window you will not open, and even death grants him no rest. The two of you haunt the heath separately, two storms that can never quite touch. It is the love you chose and the punishment you earned, indistinguishable at last.

The young lovers marry and quiet the old houses with ordinary happiness — the very thing you and Heathcliff could never manage. You let the moor have your story and the children have their peace. The wind, for once, just blows.

You never quite leave. You become the heath itself — the wind, the heather, the line where the storm meets the hill. People who walk there feel watched and loved and a little afraid, and they are right on all three counts.
